summary: Plumas NF summit lookout in the Bucks Lake Wilderness; cabins from before 1920 to 1973, buildings offered for sale in 1973, and a 2012 trip report found only concrete and cable left.

facts.design: Ground cabin before 1920; BC-201 Fireman-Lookout cabin built in 1934 to replace the older building
facts.status_note: Buildings offered for sale in 1973 on condition they be removed; a 2012 trip report found only concrete and cable

staffing.status: summer lookouts named in newspapers 1914-1963; closing year disputed (1966 in a Plumas history, budget warning in 1971)

access.note: In the Bucks Lake Wilderness; a 2012 trip report describes a spur off the Pacific Crest Trail. No current access rule found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: A wooden sign marks the spur to the summit, and the 2012 trip report calls the walk easy. No source read describes conditions after 2012.

corrections.proposed: replaced 1934 (BC-201 replaced an older building); earlier history: built 1913 per Plumas history quoted in a 2012 trip report
corrections.why: The register says the 1934 cabin replaced an older building, and the older lookout dates back to 1907 or earlier. Calling 1934 the build year understates the site's history.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says a lookout from 1907, a ground cabin before 1920, and the BC-201 in 1934. The Plumas history quoted in a 2012 trip report says built 1913, rebuilt 1922, modified 1933. The story reports both.

A Plumas history quoted in a 2012 trip report names Doris Rippy as last lookout and says the station closed December 2, 1966. A 1963 newspaper names Jean Rippey as that summer's lookout, and a 1971 item warns of discontinuing the lookout. The story reports the 1966 date as the history's claim and notes the 1971 warning.

notes_for_editor: Two conflicting histories (register vs. Plumas history quoted by a 2012 trip report) and a closing-date dispute. The Plumas history is only quoted second-hand through a blog; the book itself was not read. Do not confuse with the Oregon Spanish Peak lookout, which turned up in search results. Staffing names come from Forest Lookouts newspaper transcriptions. The record's kind 'ground' and material 'wood' are consistent with the sources.
